_README: Per-map configuration. This is the file you edit to point the block at a different dataset — it decides what the card shows and in what order, and nothing else in app/ needs touching. `actions` is the row of buttons under the name: the few things a resident is most likely to want, before any descriptive detail. `facts` are short values in rows under the address, each beside an `icon` (clock, globe, phone or info). `card` is the longer detail below them, each field under its label as a heading. `updated`, when given, names the field holding the day a site's details were last checked; without it the card shows the data's own date. `openInMaps` appends a Directions button that opens the site in Google Maps. Give it a `query` list of fields and the link searches Google for them joined with commas — here just the address, which lands the resident on Google's card for it: the pin, Street View, a Directions button and whatever businesses Google knows are there. Keep the query to the address. Adding the organization's name can upgrade that to its own Google profile, but the name is unverified spreadsheet text, and when it matches a different branch of the same organization it sends the resident to the wrong building with nothing on screen to say so. Set `openInMaps` to `true` instead and the link carries the site's coordinate, which drops an unlabelled pin and is the right choice when the addresses are too rough for a global geocoder to read. Set it false to drop the link. Individual addresses Google reads wrongly are corrected in data/overrides.json, not here. In both, `source` is "site" to read the field off the GeoJSON feature's properties, or "org" to read it off the matching record in orgs.json. Labels are written in English and looked up in app/src/i18n/<language>.json for each other language, so a new label needs its translations added there. `coLocationRadiusM` is how close two records must be, in metres, for the card to offer a stepper between them (see CO_LOCATION_RADIUS_M in app/src/logic/data.ts).
title: SNAP volunteer opportunities
